findings.place: Opening word, line 1
findings.evidence: Crop 01 shows a capital with a roof and baseline, followed by a second tall descending stroke and a detached short crossbar to its right. The last low strokes are too reduced to separate em from ou securely. The second tall/crossed form supports Item as the first reading; the alternatives remain open. H’s Ici does not account for that tall crossed form.

findings.place: Short form before application, line 3
findings.evidence: Crop 02 shows two tall strokes sharing a crossing, then a short terminal curve at the baseline. There are no separate intervening o/u bodies. The written contracted group is tte; C’s primary reading is resolved rather than changed.

findings.place: Relation between X and S-star, line 4
findings.evidence: Crop 03 shows a long near-horizontal shaft, a thickened right endpoint and a tiny downward stub. A complete two-sided arrowhead is not visible. The shaft-first transcription and arrow alternative are both retained.
findings.mathematical_note: The nearby words application surjective make an arrow a reading cue, but do not supply the missing upper head stroke.

findings.place: Two groups before images, line 4
findings.evidence: Crop 04 shows two separate ink groups before images. The first begins with a tall closed loop and has a low tail. The second has a short upright over a smaller loop, a long low continuation and a downturned end. This favors les des, with les les retained for the compressed second group. The two-group presence is clear even though its second word remains uncertain.
findings.mathematical_note: The grammatical expectation of a single article was not used to remove either group.

findings.place: Overwritten capital at Or, line 6
findings.evidence: Crop 05 shows extra underlying strokes in the O: a left upright, an internal oblique/return and a low curved outline survive beneath the darker live form. They support a possible older D, but the layers cannot be separated securely enough to make its identity and cancelled state certain. Uncertainty therefore surrounds the older deleted-D representation as a whole. The r is live and clear.

findings.place: After application, line 7

workflow_feedback: Read only the assigned brief, the supplied pre-scan notation table, scan030 packet, C/H witnesses, C context, C doubt index, supplied preamble and H style, and the three assigned images. No other page, reader output or main-reader decision was inspected.

The whole image was viewed once for layout, each provided half once for a complete ink reading, then one crop was made and viewed once for each genuinely open locus or coherent correction passage. D010 was settled from half b and was not cropped.

All twelve source boxes were checked against the original 1693 by 2365 image bounds before cropping. Processing used Pillow autocontrast, LANCZOS enlargement to 3000 pixels wide and sharpness factor 1.5; no rotation was needed. No accidental source-edge clipping occurred.

Crops include neighboring strokes for context. Crop 07 contains the family index and its interacting raised addition/leader; crop 12 contains the lower correction and final connector. Clear words incidentally visible within those context areas were not cropped again.

The clear H differences received original whole-image bounds even when no crop was made. Several such bounds were tightened through non-OCR dark-pixel extent measurement within manually identified source regions; this did not involve a further visual opening or text recognition.

H’s explicit note about interlinear deux à deux was checked against its actual ink, and no such words were seen. The H style supplies emphasis/uncertainty/addition/deletion conventions but gives no page-specific exact notation mapping requiring another change here. Macro syntax alone has not been counted as a departure.

The complete reading.tex was saved immediately after finishing the image reading and before composing this return. No compilation, OCR, PDF text extraction, external research or mathematical repair was used.
All written code/artifacts from this assignment are confined to work/readers/scan030/R1. The supplied isolated-page workflow and parent delivery instruction determine this intermediate destination.

notes.text: The upper paragraph concerns the traces of binary decompositions on the written set S-star = S amalg A-prime, then a surjective application and its indexed family of nonempty sets. It records the two families U_s and E_a. The relation sign after X and the small high mark in the family index remain graphical uncertainties. The words application and surjective, and the clearer S-star occurrences, were mathematical reading cues only.

The author explicitly writes that the case of empty U_s and E_a is “à examiner avec plus de soin”, then “il donne néanmoins ce qu'on veut”. The paragraph cites the labels (*) and (**) and uses the handwritten form sss twice. The spelling stricte and the phrase “ceci (plus fort que (**))” are preserved. No proof of the stated claims was checked.

The final labelled condition contains a visible revision: cancelled tel is accompanied by live interlinear et; the cancelled continuation que U_s=empty-set, et has the inserted edge phrase above it. The final display contains the two not-equal/empty-set comparisons separated by a reduced mark read first as ou. Its disjunctive role supplied a reading cue but the glyph remains uncertain.

The sheet contains no visible title or date and no authorial page number. The light lower-left 29 is retained as archive numbering in a TeX comment. No diagram, drawing, independent margin note, or typed substrate was observed.

workflow_feedback: Read only the assigned brief, notation table, packet, C, H, page-specific C context and doubt index, supplied preambles, and the three assigned scan images. No other pages, readers, main decisions, OCR, text recognition, external research, or compilation were used.

Whole image opened once for layout. Each supplied half opened once and read line by line. All twelve prepared crops were viewed exactly once. Each crop serves a locus still open after the halves; crop 07 coherently covers the small family index, attached insertion and cancelled à.

Crop bounds were checked against the 1693 by 2365 source before extraction. Every crop was enlarged to 3000 pixels wide with LANCZOS, autocontrast and UnsharpMask. No rotation was necessary. No target locus was clipped or recropped; surrounding context is intentionally truncated at crop boundaries.
Complete reading.tex was saved immediately after image reading, before return.json was composed. Only the R2 directory was written.
All thirteen C doubts have retained or resolved findings. Resolving a C primary reading is reported separately from a primary-reading error; no C primary reading was changed.

H's preamble and explicit page note were read. H's emphasis macro was treated as authorial underlining where stated; no finding was created from macro spelling alone. Its page note acknowledging an interlinear attachment was taken into account, while its extra words were collated against the visible insertion.
The only mathematical work was using local statement structure as a reading cue. No proof check, independent re-proof, computation or formal verification was performed, so check_events is empty.

findings.place: Opening word before comma
findings.evidence: Crop 01 shows a capital-like upright with a long baseline, a separate tall descending stem under the shared upper sweep, a short detached cross-stroke beside it, and a very low final wave. The final letters remain compressed. The tall second stem is visible; the alternatives Item, Idem and Itou remain open.

findings.place: Application phrase: word before application
findings.evidence: Crop 02 has two tall joined strokes crossed by a common bar and a short right return. There is no intervening sequence of low o/u loops. The written abbreviation tte is legible.

findings.place: Mark between X and S-star
findings.evidence: Crop 03 shows one long nearly horizontal stroke, rising slightly to the right, with a short downward spur at the thick right end. A full converging arrow point is not separable. The horizontal-stroke reading stays primary, with an incomplete arrow retained as an alternative.
findings.mathematical_note: The noun application makes an arrow a natural reading cue, but supplies no missing head in the ink.

findings.place: Two short groups immediately before images
findings.evidence: Crop 04 shows two separate groups before the dotted initial of images. The first begins with a tall loop and a low tail. The second has a small closed loop with a short upright above it and a long right tail. That second opening looks d-like, although a reduced l remains possible. Both groups are retained.

findings.place: Overwritten initial at Or
findings.evidence: Crop 05 shows a straight left upright and a broad outer right bowl beneath/among a smaller inner loop and the heavy live Or strokes. A prior D is possible, but the relative layers do not completely establish the old letter or its cancellation state. The uncertainty encloses both its identity and deletion state.

findings.place: Punctuation after telle application
findings.evidence: Crop 06 shows a detached, short black diagonal after the low ending of application. It is separated from that ending by a small blank and descends from the baseline as a comma.

findings.place: High mark on S in family subscript
findings.evidence: Crop 07 shows a very small angular high mark after S, with a rising stroke and a short rightward branch. The available strokes do not securely separate a reduced star from a plus. The primary star is retained without treating C or H as having a demonstrated primary-reading error.
findings.mathematical_note: Earlier S-star occurrences on the same page are clearer, but do not determine this small high mark.

findings.place: Cancelled short word between i.e. and celle
findings.kind: deletion state (struck given live or live given struck)
findings.evidence: Crop 07 shows a small a-like loop, a detached accent above it, and a horizontal cancellation passing through the word. Celle follows live. The reading à and its struck state are legible.

findings.place: Start of line des deux familles
findings.evidence: Crop 08 shows the looped d, the compressed middle return, and a terminal stroke that extends and then turns down/right after the middle portion. I read the terminal s and resolve the word as des, retaining C and H primary readings.

findings.place: First sss, after ce qu’on veut
findings.evidence: Half b shows three linked s-shaped forms with upward turns and no detached dot above the final form. The half settled this reading, so no crop was made for it.
findings.mathematical_note: Its position before on a les conditions is a contextual cue only; the absence of an i-dot and the repeated curved shape govern the reading.

findings.place: Inner parenthesized label after plus fort que
findings.evidence: Crop 10 separates two crossed centers inside the small inner parentheses: a thinner crossing at the left and a darker compact crossing at the right, linked by a low stroke. A larger outer closing parenthesis follows. I read two stars from those separate centers.
findings.mathematical_note: The earlier one-star and two-star labels were read independently in half b. Their order was not used to supply the count in this crowded label.

findings.place: Struck short word after underlined d’ordre 2
findings.evidence: Crop 11 shows a tall crossed first stem, a low middle loop, and a final high return under a heavy horizontal cancellation. These surviving strokes support tel. The separate live et above it is reported in F24.

findings.place: Connector in final display
findings.evidence: Crop 12 shows a low short undulation: a small raised or knotted beginning and a longer nearly flat right tail. It can support reduced ou, but the letters do not fully separate from a dash-like mark. C’s uncertainty remains.
findings.mathematical_note: Its position between the two inequalities cues a connective; it does not complete the letters.

findings.place: Interlinear abbreviation above family index
findings.evidence: Half a and crop 07 show d, a raised apostrophe-like stroke, and a short low ens group. The full word ensembles is not written. The phrase is interlinear and linked to the gap after the indexed family.

findings.place: H additional words in the interlinear insertion
findings.evidence: Half a and crop 07 show only the short d’ens group followed directly by two horizontal comparison strokes crossed by a slash, and a slashed oval. The space and ink of that interline contain no separate words deux à deux disjoints. The curved leader descends toward the end of the family.
findings.mathematical_note: The transcript does not add disjointness to the author’s short insertion. H’s prose note also calls the interline an addition; this finding concerns its extra words, not macro choice.

findings.place: Punctuation after final d’ens in first paragraph
findings.evidence: Half a and the overlapping top of half b show d’ens followed by a clear gap and non; no abbreviation period is visible in that gap. The point after vides is separately visible and retained.

findings.place: Wording after est à examiner
findings.evidence: Half b reads avec as two low linked groups, plus with a tall looped initial, de with its small loop, and soin with its separated high dot/accent-like stroke and ending before the comma. The full phrase avec plus de soin is readable from the half.

findings.place: Wording from nevertheless through ce qu’on veut
findings.evidence: Half b shows néanmoins at the right end of the line after il donne; the next line begins ce qu’on veut. The q has a long descender, the apostrophe after qu is detached, and the short final veut ends before sss. Those words are legible; there is no unreadable word at H’s ellipsis in this span.

findings.place: Second sss, after stricte
findings.evidence: Half b shows the same three curved joined forms after stricte, with no detached final i-dot. The context included in crop 09 also preserves that shape, but no extra crop was made for the settled occurrence.

findings.place: Ending of adjective after non-parallélisme
findings.evidence: Crop 09 shows the initial loop and tall crossed t, low r/i strokes, a broad low c-return, another upright crossed t, and a final separate low rightward curl after that t. That final curl supports the written terminal e.
findings.mathematical_note: The adjective’s written terminal e is retained beside the noun non-parallélisme; no agreement repair is made.

notes.text: The opening discusses traces of the binary decompositions on S-star = S amalgam A-prime and a surjective application from X. The manuscript starts a phrase with si on regarde and later begins Donc; no missing principal verb has been supplied. The long mark after X is retained as a horizontal-stroke/arrow uncertainty.

The next part records an indexed family (X_sigma) and the two families (U_s) and (E_a). The repeated small sigma has a circular body and extended roof in both positions. The interline says d’ens ≠∅ and has a curved attachment to the end of the first family. No words asserting disjointness are visible there.

The author writes that the case of empty component sets is « à examiner avec plus de soin ». The continuation reads « il donne néanmoins ce qu’on veut » and cites (*) and (**). The same paragraph writes non-parallélisme stricte, sss, and underlined ceci, followed by plus fort que (**). These are reported statements; no proof check was performed.

At the foot, the (***) passage names a vertex s∈S, underlines d’ordre 2, replaces struck tel by upper et, and places a∈A une arête incidente, on a above the cancelled que U_s=∅, et. The live display contains two slashed comparison signs. The middle connector and the final E subscript remain uncertain. The old equality and the live inequalities were read as ink, without mathematical repair.
The sheet has archive pencil number 29 at the lower left. No separate author page number, title, or date was visible. No drawing, diagram, or independent margin note was present.

Mathematical reading cues were limited to identifying repeated sigma shapes, comparing the page’s clearer S-star occurrences with the small family-index mark, noting the use of labels (*), (**), (***), comparing the old equality with the live slashed comparisons, and recognizing that the earlier E_a and a∈A make a relevant to the open final subscript. No cue was used to supply a missing stroke or change a written statement.

readers.check_events_note: No mathematical proof check, computation, re-proof or formal certificate was performed. Reading and symbol comparison were not counted as proof checks.
